## Purpose

Assigns each population an NHDPlusV2 COMID using a local copy of the
NHDPlusV2.1 national seamless geodatabase. Everything runs offline against a
fixed data version, so results are reproducible.

For each population:

1. **Catchment COMID:** the NHDPlusV2 catchment polygon the point falls in.
   This is the COMID used downstream, because the `lc_` landscape variables
   summarise the local catchment.
2. **Offset to its own flowline:** straight-line distance (m) from the point
   to the flowline of that catchment, used for the distance cutoff.
3. **Nearest flowline:** the COMID and distance of the closest network
   flowline, used only to flag points where the nearest stream belongs to a
   different catchment (usually near confluences or catchment edges).

The output is a lookup table keyed by `Pop_id`. It contains no genetic data
and is joined to everything else in the final assembly script.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(sf)
library(nhdplusTools)
library(tigris)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)               # all geometry work is planar in EPSG:5070
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
pct <- function(x, n) paste0(round(100 * x / n, 1), "%")
```

```{r}
#| label: paths
path_pops    <- here("Data", "interim", "GenDiv_merged.csv")
dir_nhd      <- here("Data", "external", "nhdplusv2")
path_out     <- here("Data", "interim", "comid_lookup.csv")
```

```{r}
#| label: parameters
crs_work      <- 5070                    # CONUS Albers, metres
crs_nhd       <- st_crs(4269)            # NAD83; CRS of the national seamless gdb
max_offset_m  <- 1000                    # same cutoff as the original pipeline
search_m      <- 2 * max_offset_m        # search wider than the cutoff to see near misses
aoi_buffer_m  <- search_m + 1000         # area read from the gdb around each point

# Set to TRUE once to download (~7.8 GB). Extraction uses the archive
# package, so 7-Zip isn't required.
download_if_missing <- FALSE
```

## NHDPlusV2 national data

```{r}
#| label: locate-gdb
find_gdb <- function(dir) {
  if (!dir.exists(dir)) return(character(0))
  list.files(dir, pattern = "\\.gdb$", recursive = TRUE,
             include.dirs = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
}

find_7z <- function(dir) {
  if (!dir.exists(dir)) return(character(0))
  list.files(dir, pattern = "\\.7z$", full.names = TRUE)
}

gdb <- find_gdb(dir_nhd)

if (length(gdb) == 0) {
  # Download only if there's no archive already sitting in dir_nhd
  if (length(find_7z(dir_nhd)) == 0) {
    if (!download_if_missing) {
      stop("No NHDPlusV2 geodatabase or archive found in ", dir_nhd,
           ". Set download_if_missing <- TRUE to download it.")
    }
    dir.create(dir_nhd, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    # nhdplusTools also tries to extract with 7-Zip; if 7-Zip isn't
    # installed it leaves the .7z in place, which is extracted below
    tryCatch(download_nhdplusv2(outdir = dir_nhd), error = function(e) NULL)
  }

  archive_7z <- find_7z(dir_nhd)
  stopifnot("Expected exactly one .7z archive in dir_nhd" = length(archive_7z) == 1)

  # Extract with libarchive; no 7-Zip install needed. Slow and needs free
  # disk space well beyond the archive's size.
  archive::archive_extract(archive_7z, dir = dir_nhd)
  gdb <- find_gdb(dir_nhd)
}

stopifnot("Expected exactly one .gdb in dir_nhd" = length(gdb) == 1)

layers <- st_layers(gdb)$name
stopifnot(
  "Catchment layer not found"           = "Catchment" %in% layers,
  "NHDFlowline_Network layer not found" = "NHDFlowline_Network" %in% layers
)
```

Using **`r basename(gdb)`**.

## Populations

```{r}
#| label: read-pops
pops <- read_csv(path_pops, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(Pop_id, Study_id, Latitude, Longitude)

stopifnot("Pop_id is not unique" = !anyDuplicated(pops$Pop_id))

pops_sf <- st_as_sf(pops, coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326,
                    remove = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(crs_work)
```

There are **`r fmt(nrow(pops))`** populations from
**`r fmt(n_distinct(pops$Study_id))`** studies to snap.

## Read NHDPlusV2 around the populations

Only catchments and flowlines near a population are read. Populations are
grouped into grid tiles, and each tile is read with a small rectangular
filter, which the geodatabase's spatial index can answer quickly. (A single
filter shaped like all the buffered points spans the whole country, so GDAL
ends up scanning and testing every catchment in the nation.)

```{r}
#| label: aoi-tiles
tile_size_deg <- 0.5

# One rectangle (in the gdb's CRS) per occupied tile, covering that tile's
# buffered points
tile_boxes <- pops_sf |>
  mutate(tile = paste(floor(Longitude / tile_size_deg),
                      floor(Latitude / tile_size_deg))) |>
  st_buffer(aoi_buffer_m) |>
  st_transform(crs_nhd) |>
  split(~tile) |>
  lapply(\(x) st_as_text(st_as_sfc(st_bbox(x))))
```

The populations fall in **`r fmt(length(tile_boxes))`** tiles.

```{r}
#| label: read-nhd
# Use ring orientation (ESRI convention) to build multipart polygons instead
# of GDAL's slow default geometric test
Sys.setenv(OGR_ORGANIZE_POLYGONS = "ONLY_CCW")

read_tiles <- function(layer, id_col) {
  lapply(tile_boxes, \(b) st_read(gdb, layer = layer, wkt_filter = b,
                                  quiet = TRUE) |>
           st_zm()) |>                           # flowlines carry Z/M values
    do.call(what = rbind) |>
    distinct(.data[[id_col]], .keep_all = TRUE)   # tiles overlap at edges
}

catchments <- read_tiles("Catchment", "FEATUREID")
flowlines  <- read_tiles("NHDFlowline_Network", "COMID")

stopifnot(
  "Unexpected CRS in gdb; update crs_nhd" = st_crs(catchments) == crs_nhd,
  "FEATUREID missing from catchments"     = "FEATUREID" %in% names(catchments),
  "COMID missing from flowlines"          = "COMID" %in% names(flowlines)
)

catchments <- catchments |>
  select(comid = FEATUREID) |>
  st_transform(crs_work) |>
  st_make_valid()

flowlines <- flowlines |>
  st_zm() |>
  select(COMID) |>
  st_transform(crs_work)
```

Read **`r fmt(nrow(catchments))`** catchments and
**`r fmt(nrow(flowlines))`** network flowlines.

## Step 1 — Catchment containing each point

```{r}
#| label: catchment-join
catch_hits <- pops_sf |>
  select(Pop_id) |>
  st_join(catchments, join = st_intersects, left = TRUE) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(Pop_id) |>
  summarise(
    n_catchments = sum(!is.na(comid)),
    comid        = first(comid),     # points on a shared edge: keep the first
    .groups      = "drop"
  )
```

**`r fmt(sum(catch_hits$n_catchments > 0))`** populations
(`r pct(sum(catch_hits$n_catchments > 0), nrow(pops))`) fall inside an
NHDPlusV2 catchment; **`r fmt(sum(catch_hits$n_catchments == 0))`** do not.
`r fmt(sum(catch_hits$n_catchments > 1))` sit exactly on a boundary between
catchments and were assigned the first match.

## Step 2 — Distance to flowlines

```{r}
#| label: flowline-index
# Nearest network flowline; kept only if within search_m
i_near <- st_nearest_feature(pops_sf, flowlines)

nearest <- tibble(
  Pop_id           = pops_sf$Pop_id,
  comid_nearest    = flowlines$COMID[i_near],
  offset_nearest_m = as.numeric(st_distance(pops_sf, flowlines[i_near, ],
                                            by_element = TRUE))
) |>
  filter(offset_nearest_m <= search_m)

# Distance to the flowline of the point's own catchment
own <- catch_hits |>
  filter(!is.na(comid)) |>
  mutate(has_flowline = comid %in% flowlines$COMID)

own$offset_own_m <- NA_real_
i <- own$has_flowline
own$offset_own_m[i] <- as.numeric(st_distance(
  pops_sf[match(own$Pop_id[i], pops_sf$Pop_id), ],
  flowlines[match(own$comid[i], flowlines$COMID), ],
  by_element = TRUE
))
```

`r fmt(sum(!own$has_flowline))` of the catchments containing a population
have no network flowline (e.g., isolated sinks or coastal catchments), so
those populations get no offset.

## Classify and apply the distance cutoff

```{r}
#| label: classify
lookup <- pops |>
  select(Pop_id, Study_id) |>
  left_join(catch_hits, by = "Pop_id") |>
  left_join(select(own, Pop_id, offset_own_m), by = "Pop_id") |>
  left_join(nearest, by = "Pop_id") |>
  mutate(
    status = case_when(
      is.na(comid)                     ~ "no_catchment",
      is.na(offset_own_m)              ~ "no_flowline",
      offset_own_m > max_offset_m      ~ "too_far",
      comid != comid_nearest |
        is.na(comid_nearest)           ~ "nearest_differs",
      TRUE                             ~ "ok"
    ),
    retained = status %in% c("ok", "nearest_differs")
  )

stopifnot(
  "Rows lost or duplicated" = nrow(lookup) == nrow(pops),
  "Pop_id duplicated"       = !anyDuplicated(lookup$Pop_id)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: status-summary
lookup |>
  count(status, retained, name = "populations") |>
  mutate(share = pct(populations, nrow(lookup))) |>
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

**`r fmt(sum(lookup$retained))`** populations
(`r pct(sum(lookup$retained), nrow(lookup))`) from
**`r fmt(n_distinct(lookup$Study_id[lookup$retained]))`** studies pass:

- `r fmt(sum(lookup$status == "no_catchment"))` are outside every catchment
  (typically Great Lakes open water, large estuaries or the coast).
- `r fmt(sum(lookup$status == "no_flowline"))` are in a catchment without a
  network flowline.
- `r fmt(sum(lookup$status == "too_far"))` are more than
  `r fmt(max_offset_m)` m from their catchment's flowline.
- `r fmt(sum(lookup$status == "nearest_differs"))` are retained, but the
  nearest flowline belongs to a different catchment. These are worth checking
  on a map.

Populations sharing a COMID after snapping:
`r fmt(sum(table(lookup$comid[lookup$retained]) > 1))` COMIDs hold more than
one retained population.

## Map

```{r}
#| label: map
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5
states <- tigris::states(cb = TRUE, year = 2023, progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  filter(!STUSPS %in% c("HI", "PR", "AK", "MP", "GU", "AS", "VI")) |>
  st_transform(crs_work)

map_dat <- pops_sf |>
  left_join(select(lookup, Pop_id, status), by = "Pop_id")

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = "white") +
  geom_sf(data = map_dat, aes(color = status), size = 1.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    ok              = "grey55",
    nearest_differs = "#E69F00",
    too_far         = "#D55E00",
    no_flowline     = "#CC79A7",
    no_catchment    = "#0072B2"
  )) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Write output

```{r}
#| label: write-output
lookup |>
  select(Pop_id, comid, comid_nearest, offset_own_m, offset_nearest_m,
         n_catchments, status, retained) |>
  mutate(nhdplus_source = basename(gdb)) |>
  write_csv(path_out)
```

Wrote **`r fmt(nrow(lookup))`** rows to `r basename(path_out)`. All
populations are kept in the lookup, with `retained` marking those that pass;
the final assembly script filters on it.
